claim: Foreman's standard handoff profile carries 68 words of fixed guardrail text against the reinforced profile's 567 — 12% of it, 499 words saved on every standard handoff.

fixtures.role: the canonical template both profiles are assembled from — the measured text
supplies the required-block definitions, so the measurement cannot drift from the gate that enforces them
computes the number; promptOverhead() is the exported entry point

aggregate.statistic: single deterministic computation (no dispersion — repeating it returns the same values)

limitations: This is a static computation over files in the repository, not a model trial. No session ran, no tokens were spent, and nothing here says a shorter handoff produces better or cheaper work.
Words, not tokens. The ratio is a proxy for context cost, not a measurement of it — tokenization is not proportional to word count.

Fixed guardrail text only. Per-task content (task context, relevant files, task rules) is the same job described the same way in either profile, so it is excluded from both sides; a real assembled handoff is longer than these numbers on both arms and the ratio between two real handoffs is therefore higher.

The reinforced profile's tone and output-format blocks are not counted: they are required present but their text is per-task, and the template's defaults sit behind bracketed instruction lines that never reach an assembled prompt.

Republished from R-009 when the health tools moved from benchmarks/health/ into the shipped scripts/health/ (the benchmark harness left the plugin for the marketplace repo). Only attention-cost.js's require paths changed; the counted guardrail text and both profiles are untouched, so the numbers are identical to R-009's — this record exists to pin them to the current file bytes, not to report a movement.
Valid only for the fixtures at the sha256 values recorded above. Editing any of them changes the number and invalidates this record — validate-records.js fails rather than letting the claim drift.
environment.foreman_commit names the PARENT commit. This record ships in the same commit as the fixture edits it measures.
